city_tips.title: Use Shanghai's extensive metro system
city_tips.content: Shanghai's public transport network is anchored by one of the world's most extensive metro systems, clean, fast, and affordable.
city_tips.evidence: Shanghai has an excellent public transport network with the one of the world's most extensive metro (subway and elevated train) systems as its backbone

city_tips.title: Get a Shanghai Jiaotong Card for transit
city_tips.content: The Jiaotong transit card lets you change lines at certain stations without needing another ticket, on top of the usual bus and metro discounts.

city_tips.title: Shanghai is very safe for solo travelers

city_tips.content: The Beijing Subway has many lines and stations covering the city with affordable fares.

city_tips.title: Beijing is safe but watch for tourist scams
city_tips.content: Violent crime is rare but tourists should be cautious of taxi scams.
city_tips.evidence: Beijing, despite its size, is a very safe city, with violent crime being incredibly rare.

city_tips.title: Buy a Yang Cheng Tong card for transit
city_tips.content: A stored value card that works on metro, buses and taxis with discount rates.
city_tips.evidence: If you intend to stay in Guangzhou for a long time, buy a multi-purpose Lingnan Pass - Yang Cheng Tong () stored value card, similar to the Octopus Card in Hong Kong.

city_tips.title: Experience authentic Cantonese cuisine
city_tips.content: Guangzhou is famous for Cantonese food, dim sum and fresh seafood.
city_tips.evidence: Cantonese cuisine is well known for its blend of color, fragrance, taste and presentation, and it is ranked among the top four in the country.

city_tips.title: Guangzhou is generally safe for tourists
city_tips.content: Violent crime is rare and the crime rate compares favorably with Western cities.
city_tips.evidence: Despite its reputation among the Chinese for being crime-ridden during the 90s, Guangzhou's crime rate compares favorably with any Western city of similar size, and violent crime is very rare.
